generation.hypothesis: Accelerated high-temperature tribo-corrosion will arise from repeated formation, fracture, and removal of discontinuous oxide/tribo-layer patches, rather than from corrosion or mechanical wear acting independently. AlCoCrFeNi2.1 should resist this coupling better than duplex stainless steel 2205 because its thermally stable lamellar microstructure should maintain homogeneous Cr availability and rapid passive-film repair.
generation.material_initial_state: Mirror-polished, as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 containing about 70% L12 and 30% B2 in a fine lamellar structure, with 2–3 µm B2 lamellae and nanoscale Cr-rich precipitates, will be compared with hot-rolled DS2205 containing approximately equal γ-FCC austenite and δ-BCC ferrite.
generation.intervention: Both alloys will receive three rapid heating/quenching cycles to about 1100 °C, followed by immersed reciprocating tribo-corrosion against alumina. The controlled comparison will match thermal conditioning, temperature, load, frequency, counter-body, and aqueous environment.
generation.conditions: Tests will use deionized water at 25, 50, and 100 °C, loads of 5–15 N, frequencies of 3–9 Hz, and a 3.5 mm stroke. The principal temperature comparison will use 5 N and 5 Hz, with post-sliding immersion to assess repassivation.
generation.structural_mediator: The HEA should retain near-initial L12/B2 fractions, whereas DS2205 could undergo substantial γ-to-δ redistribution. The interfacial mediator should shift from abrasive contact at 25 °C, to a stable passive film or compacted low-shear tribo-layer near 50 °C, and to discontinuous, mechanically unstable oxide patches at 100 °C.
generation.mechanism: At 25 °C, relatively slow film repair should permit two-body abrasion. Near 50 °C, thermally accelerated repassivation without extensive brittle-film disruption should promote polishing wear and minimum loss. At 100 °C, repeated film growth, rupture, and entrainment as debris should produce oxidative or third-body wear, friction instability, and coupled degradation.
generation.predicted_outcome: The HEA should undergo only a few percent phase redistribution, versus roughly 35 percentage points of γ-to-δ change in DS2205. Its wear rate should be about one order of magnitude lower, with lower friction: approximately 0.2, 0.18, and 0.25 at 25, 50, and 100 °C, compared with roughly 0.4, 0.32, and 0.4 for DS2205. For both alloys, total wear-volume loss should follow 50 °C < 25 °C < 100 °C. The HEA should also show nobler, steadier open-circuit potential, faster repassivation, and higher polarization resistance.
generation.baseline: DS2205 under identical conditioning and sliding conditions will be the primary baseline; 25 °C and the as-cast phase fractions will provide within-alloy environmental and structural references.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis will apply to transient thermal-shock conditioning and reciprocating contact in low-ionic-strength water over 25–100 °C, 5–15 N, and 3–9 Hz. It will not establish equilibrium or continuous-service stability at 1100 °C, oxidation kinetics, or behavior in chloride-, sulfate-, or other ion-containing industrial waters.
generation.uncertainty: The extent to which the 50 °C minimum depends on tribo-layer compaction rather than passive-film electrochemistry may remain uncertain.
